title: Flat pullback of the Rees algebra
statement: The map $\beta_g$ is a graded algebra equivalence.

proof.text: Use the data of [def-nagata-flat-pullback-rees-map]: a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ and a flat morphism $g:Y\to X$. For every $n\geq0$, apply exactness in [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-pullback-exact-pushforward-injective] to the inclusion $\mathcal I^n\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_X$. Thus $g^*\mathcal I^n\to g^*\mathcal O_X$ is injective. The tensor formula in [def-pc-module-pullback] identifies $g^*\mathcal O_X$ with $\mathcal O_Y$: locally $b\otimes a\mapsto b g^\sharp(a)$ has inverse $b\mapsto b\otimes1$, since $b\otimes a=b g^\sharp(a)\otimes1$. By [lemma-nagata-flat-pullback-ideal-pow], the image in $\mathcal O_Y$ is exactly $(\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y)^n$. Consequently its factorization onto that image is an isomorphism $e_n:g^*\mathcal I^n\xrightarrow{\sim}(\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y)^n$. This is precisely the canonical degree-$n$ map defining $\beta_g$, rather than an arbitrarily chosen isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 02N4, lemma-pullback-flat; blueprint comparison in each degree

proof.text: The adjunction $g^*\dashv g_*$ stated in [def-pc-module-pullback], together with [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] applied to the small discrete category $\mathbf N$, identifies $g^*(\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal I^n)$ with $\bigoplus_{n\geq0}g^*\mathcal I^n$. The source direct sum exists by [def-nagata-sheaf-rees-algebra]; the colimit lemma also supplies its pulled-back coproduct. The target is $\bigoplus_{n\geq0}(\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y)^n$ by the same Rees definition. Under this identification, [def-nagata-flat-pullback-rees-map] identifies $\beta_g$ with the direct sum of the maps $e_n$ from step 1. The coproduct map whose restriction to the $n$th summand is $e_n^{-1}$ is an inverse: either composite restricts to the identity on every summand, hence is the identity by the coproduct universal property. This proves invertibility of the underlying module-sheaf map and preserves every degree.

source.place: Tag 0038, lemma-adjoint-exact (1); Tag 0096, lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules; assembly of the degreewise maps

proof.text: Check the algebra operations on homogeneous tensor generators. In the tensor presentation of [def-pc-module-pullback] and [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], take local $a\in\mathcal I^m$, $c\in\mathcal I^n$ and local coefficients $b,d\in\mathcal O_Y$. By [def-nagata-flat-pullback-rees-map], $e_m(b\otimes a)=b g^\sharp(a)$ and $e_n(d\otimes c)=d g^\sharp(c)$. The multiplication of [def-nagata-sheaf-rees-algebra] sends their source product to $bd\otimes ac$, so both routes give $bd g^\sharp(ac)=b g^\sharp(a)d g^\sharp(c)$ in degree $m+n$. Bilinearity extends this equality to finite sums of pure tensors and then to their sheafifications. The degree-zero element $1\otimes1$ maps to $1$, and degree-zero scalars $b\otimes1$ map to $b$. Thus the map already shown invertible is a unital graded $\mathcal O_Y$-algebra morphism.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product (definition by sheafification); blueprint instruction to check compatibility with multiplication

proof.text: Let $E$ be the inverse module-sheaf map constructed in step 2. For local sections $u,v$ of the target algebra, multiplicativity in step 3 gives $\beta_g(E(u)E(v))=uv=\beta_g(E(uv))$. Apply the inverse $E$ to obtain $E(u)E(v)=E(uv)$; similarly $\beta_g(E(1))=1=\beta_g(1)$ gives $E(1)=1$. Its module linearity supplies preservation of addition and scalars, and its degree-$n$ restriction is $e_n^{-1}$. Therefore $E$ is a graded algebra inverse of $\beta_g$, proving the claimed equivalence.

Step 1: the ideal-pow statement gives only the image equality, so injectivity of g^*I^n -> g^*O_X = O_Y comes from flat-pullback exactness (lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-pullback-exact-pushforward-injective, true by Stacks 02N4 modules.tex:3191). This correctly avoids using ideal-pow's proof (C3), and e_n is the canonical degree-n map. Step 2: g^* is a left adjoint (def-pc-module-pullback), so the Mathlib leaf leftAdjoint_preservesColimits gives preservation of the sum over the discrete N; the inverse is the sum of the e_n^{-1} by the coproduct universal property. Step 4: the inverse of a bijective algebra map is an algebra map. Edge cases checked: n=0, I=0, I=O_X, nilpotent I, non-surjective flat g. Z->Z/2 with I=(2) shows flatness is needed.
